subject.title: [Feature]: Support for Custom Emojis in Latest Telegram Bot API Update

question: What permanent API shape should OpenClaw expose for Telegram custom emoji delivery: raw Telegram entities, a shared rich-text/custom-emoji IR, Telegram-owned channel data, or a combination?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but exposing entity arrays changes shared message-tool and plugin API shape while Telegram delivery must preserve chunking, caption, edit, and fallback semantics.

options.title: Shared Rich-Text Representation
options.body: Add a typed representation that can carry custom emoji IDs through the shared message tool and let Telegram map it to Bot API entities or safe HTML.

options.title: Telegram-Owned Entities
options.body: Add a narrow `channelData.telegram.entities` and `caption_entities` path with Telegram-specific validation and focused tests.

options.title: HTML-Only Scope
options.body: Declare `<tg-emoji>` HTML passthrough the supported path and keep raw entity-array requests out of scope for now.

recommendation.title: Shared Rich-Text Representation
recommendation.body: Add a typed representation that can carry custom emoji IDs through the shared message tool and let Telegram map it to Bot API entities or safe HTML.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior review already routed this as a shared message-tool and Telegram plugin API-shape decision.
